title: Taxat Canonical Primitives Atlas
basisStatement: Identifiers, hashes, exact decimals, and time values now share one deterministic substrate across TypeScript, Python, and validator-grounded request identity formulas.

parity_rows.label: Identifier literal parity
notes: Both runtimes preserve lawful punctuation.
Neither runtime invents regex-only narrowing in the shared primitive layer.
Do not impose slug-only or UUID-only assumptions unless a specific schema requires them.
Identifiers stay serializable as plain strings at contract boundaries.
Refs often carry lineage or locator meaning and must stay distinguishable from entity IDs.
Schema families may permit provider-flavored values that the shared layer must not over-constrain.
Hash branding distinguishes digest artifacts from plain refs or IDs even though the wire type remains string.
The shared layer does not assume a prefix like sha256: unless a contract says so.
Route tokens remain legal strings because atlas and shell routes are path-bearing by design.
The shared layer brands them without claiming ownership of router-specific parsing.
banned_patterns: Do not coerce numbers into identifier strings.
Do not add family-specific regexes inside the shared primitive layer.
Do not strip separators from refs for cosmetic normalization.
Do not assume refs can be used interchangeably with IDs.
Do not derive digests from locale-formatted or whitespace-rich stringification.
Do not treat any non-empty hash string as proof of canonicality without using the hash helpers.
Do not derive authority from breadcrumbs or human labels.
Do not normalize away routing punctuation that a router or storage boundary preserves.

families.label: HASHES
families.rail_summary: Canonical hashes use SHA-256 over deterministic JSON with Unicode NFC normalization, lexicographically ordered object keys, preserved array order, and explicit nulls.

hero.title: Canonical JSON becomes replay-safe SHA-256
hero.caption: Objects reorder, strings normalize to NFC, arrays keep declared order, and digests stay lowercase hex.

parity_rows.label: Authority request hash parity
notes: Request identity formulas stay aligned with the validator oracle.
duplicate_meaning_key and idempotency_key match as well.
Strings normalize to NFC before emission.
Objects reject duplicate normalized keys.
Digest output is lowercase hexadecimal.
Used by request, replay, and config-surface identity records.
Keys are sorted lexicographically.
Value arrays preserve declared order.
Missing or empty path parameters fail closed.
Resolved values use RFC 3986 encoding.
Business partition refs remain in declared order unless a caller explicitly sorts a set-like source.
Shares the identity namespace hash seed with request_hash and idempotency_key.
banned_patterns: Never sort legally ordered arrays before hashing.
Never hash pretty-printed JSON or locale-formatted strings.

Replay-safe hashing and normalized payload expectations are binding for manifest and execution truth.
